why: Rolls a failed import back by writing each previous value straight back -- the same setItem that just threw, on a storage no emptier than when it threw. A full storage therefore restores nothing. Also leaves keys the save never had sitting in storage, because the restore pass delegates the absent-key case to this removal. Pinned by a byte-quota fixture; a throw-after-N-writes stub cannot see this, because it refuses the rollback's writes too.
killedBy: importSave atomicity (issue #250) a key that had NO previous value is removed rather than left behind
importSave atomicity (issue #250) frees the space the failed import consumed, so a LONGER previous value fits again
